vowelSignsNote: Canonical vowels are short (a, i, u), which matches the most Dakshina romanisations; the long forms (aa, ee, oo) fold to the same skeleton.
about: Hindi (Devanagari) to Hinglish, the way people type it. Training only: training/mlkb/data/table_romanise.py samples synthetic spellings from it for transliterator pairs. It is richer than the pack file (schwa deletion, nasalised vowels, finalRewrites), which format 1 cannot express. The pack's romanisation.json (format 1) keys hinglish.fst and is what the engine reads. All text is NFC: a nukta letter is its consonant plus U+093C.

schwa.about: The inherent vowel is written 'a' unless deleted. Final: dropped after a single consonant in a word of two or more syllables (bhaarat); kept after a conjunct (mitra) and in one-letter words (na). Medial: scanning right to left, a schwa is dropped in V C _ C V (kamraa, samajhnaa, bachpan), where the consonant before it is single, the one after it is single and carries a vowel that is not itself dropped, and the schwa carries no anusvara or chandrabindu.

skeleton.about: Collapses the Latin spellings people type inconsistently, for typed text and for each word's canonical romanisation alike. In order: lowercase and keep only a-z; drop a trailing h after a vowel (nahih); left to right, apply the longest rewrite that matches, else the single-letter map (a letter it lacks maps to itself), and with collapseRuns write a run of the same output letter once; drop each letter of dropBetweenConsonants that has a consonant on both sides (samajhna, samjhna and samajna all become smjn); replace one ending of finalRewrites if the word is longer than it; drop a trailing letter of stripFinal after a consonant.
